markdown_report:
The first experiment should test a **context-conditioned soft-reset GRU**. This preserves GRU4Rec while targeting stale interests and weak connections to current activity. Improvement remains a hypothesis requiring pinned validation.

### Insights and framework

Three baseline insights guide selection. First, users reject revived older interests and media lacking specific connections; selective state retention could improve current-intent representation. Second, Electronics has 9.7% negative-over-positive comparisons and a 0.0265 lower-decile margin, motivating better discrimination of ambiguous contexts. Third, collapse scores near 0.5 imply approximately zero mean cosine similarity, so embedding-collapse regularization lacks diagnostic support.

Three literature insights define complementary directions. MTAM [1] supports learned recurrent gating, although its temporal mechanism does not validate the proposed item-conditioned reset. GRU4Rec [2] supports objectives emphasizing competitive negatives, while harder negatives introduce false-positive ambiguity. Recformer [3] motivates recommendation-specific text representations, but its pretrained Transformer recipe does not transfer directly to this constrained experiment.

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Compatible hypothesis | Principal uncertainty |
|---|---|---|---|
| State retention | MTAM temporal gates | Item/state-conditioned soft reset | Useful older preferences may disappear |
| Ranking objective | GRU4Rec BPR-max | Regularized competitive-negative learning | Hard negatives may be relevant |
| Item representation | Recformer text integration | Jointly trained title residual | Broad word overlap may dominate |

### Candidate assessments

Scores are originality / future potential / user alignment / model alignment / implementation difficulty; higher difficulty means harder. Each assessment gives a positive and negative reason.

- **Soft-reset GRU: 5/7/8/6/3.** Originality: targeted adaptation; gating is established. Potential: reusable retention mechanism; benefits may be dataset-specific. User alignment: addresses stale interests and weak current connections; cannot establish compatibility. Model alignment: may resolve ambiguous Electronics contexts; no measured gain yet. Difficulty: small recurrent change; sequential execution needs profiling.
- **BPR-max: 2/6/5/8/3.** Originality: useful transfer; established objective. Potential: inexpensive ranking improvement; limited architectural insight. User alignment: challenges broad distractors; does not represent current intent explicitly. Model alignment: directly emphasizes competitive negatives; sampled margins need not predict HR@10. Difficulty: localized loss change; collision masking needs care.
- **Title residual: 4/7/7/5/5.** Originality: constrained adaptation; text fusion is established. Potential: transfers supervision across sparse items; metadata may be noisy. User alignment: supplies artist/purpose connections; lexical overlap cannot prove fit. Model alignment: may improve ambiguous items; may also increase confusion. Difficulty: simple pooling; vocabulary and predictor serialization add work.

### Selected experiment

At 0% progress, soft-reset GRU offers a small architectural intervention. Before each valid interaction, learn vector retention from the current item and previous hidden state, then perform the ordinary GRU update. Initialize retention near one. This explicitly targets **revived older interests** and **recommendations weakly connected to recent activity**, while testing whether context ambiguity contributes to Electronics’ weak margins.

Keep the baseline loss and sampling initially. Preserve padding-masked updates, final-nonpadding readout, diagnostic interfaces, and identical training/predictor architecture. Train one checkpoint per category under the fixed seeds and limits. Select solely by macro validation HR@10; use margins as supporting diagnostics.

References: [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598), [2](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf), [3](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~jmcauley/pdfs/kdd23b.pdf).

idea.description: Add a jointly trained, item-and-state-conditioned soft-retention gate before each GRU4Rec recurrent update. Retain the original scoring head, objective, and negative sampling for the first controlled experiment.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale interests and weak connections to recent activity. Selective retention may suppress irrelevant historical state while preserving coherent preferences. Electronics’ near-zero lower-decile margin motivates testing whether improved context representation separates confusing candidates. These are hypotheses, not established improvements.
idea.implementation_notes: Use a vector gate sigmoid(W_e e_t + W_h h_previous + b), initialized with small weights and b approximately 3. Apply the gate to the previous hidden state before the GRUCell update. Skip padding updates and zero padded output positions. Compute gates only from available prefix items and hidden states; never use the next-item target. Preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), and the actual trained nn.Module exposed through ModelView. No timestamps or metadata are required for this initial variant. Update the embedded predictor writer and checkpoint configuration together. For left-padded input, gather the greatest index containing a nonzero item, with a safe all-padding fallback. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis); retain measured metrics and their definitions without inventing metadata categories or simulator traits. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], artifact paths beneath the trial directory, all four category routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Each category uses one independently trained checkpoint on a single GPU. Compare against the supplied baseline using only the pinned macro validation HR@10; do not claim that improved training margins demonstrate validation gains.
idea.pseudocode:
class SoftResetGRU:
    log2feats(sequence):
        h = zeros(batch_size, hidden_dim)
        outputs = []
        for t in range(sequence_length):
            valid = sequence[:, t] != 0
            e = baseline_input_transform(item_emb(sequence[:, t]))
            retention = sigmoid(W_e(e) + W_h(h) + gate_bias)
            proposed = gru_cell(e, retention * h)
            h = where(valid[:, None], proposed, h)
            outputs.append(where(valid[:, None], h, zeros_like(h)))
        return baseline_output_transform(stack(outputs, dim=1))

    predict_score(features, items):
        return baseline_scoring_head(features, items)

for category in FOUR_FIXED_CATEGORIES:
    seed_training(42)
    model = SoftResetGRU(baseline_configuration)
    for epoch in range(MAX_EPOCHS_AT_MOST_200):
        for batch in range(200):
            sequence, positive, negative = family_specific_sample_batch()
            features = model.log2feats(sequence)
            loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(features, positive, negative)
            optimize(loss)
        evaluate_with_fixed_validation_protocol()
    save_one_selected_checkpoint_and_matching_predictor_configuration()

# Inference: last_index = max(where(sequence != 0, position, -1)).
# Gather that position, safely handling all-padding sequences; never use count-1.

originality.positive: A focused adaptation of recurrent retention to the supplied current-intent failure patterns, preserving the GRU backbone.
originality.negative: Learned gates and recurrent state retention are established mechanisms; novelty is limited.

future_potential.positive: A successful controlled result could motivate later investigation of observed time gaps and interpretable retention behavior.
future_potential.negative: Interaction histories alone cannot establish actual product compatibility, redundant functionality, or current need.

code_difficulty.positive: Adds two projections and a sigmoid around the existing GRU recurrence without requiring extra data.
code_difficulty.negative: Explicit recurrent execution may reduce throughput, and predictor serialization must match training exactly.

related_work.title: MTAM: temporal gating for sequential recommendation
contributions: Introduces temporal gates into recurrent transitions to represent short-term intent.
Provides architectural motivation for learning selective state retention.
limitations: Does not establish the effectiveness of the proposed item-and-state-conditioned reset on this benchmark.
Temporal gating evidence does not justify hard resets after long gaps.

related_work.title: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Develops ranking objectives including BPR-max that emphasize high-scoring negatives.
Provides a compatible alternative direction for improving GRU4Rec discrimination.
limitations: Does not establish superiority under the pinned four-category validation protocol.
Competitive negative sampling cannot reliably distinguish unobserved relevant items.

related_work.title: Recformer
contributions: Motivates learning text representations aligned with recommendation objectives.
Suggests that item text can provide shared preference signals.
limitations: Its Transformer architecture and pretraining recipe are outside this GRU-only experiment.
Does not demonstrate that title pooling trained from scratch improves the supplied baseline.
